title: The Covenant of Marriage
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The covenant of marriage is God’s design for one man and one woman joined together in lifelong faithfulness. Marriage is not merely a contract, arrangement, or romantic partnership, but a covenant before God that reflects love, faithfulness, unity, and holy responsibility.
summary: The covenant of marriage is God’s design for one man and one woman joined together in lifelong faithfulness. Marriage is not merely a contract, arrangement, or romantic partnership, but a covenant before God that reflects love, faithfulness, unity, and holy responsibility.
christFocus: Marriage points beyond itself to Christ’s faithful love for His people. The love of a husband for his wife is called to reflect Christ’s sacrificial love for the church, and the faithfulness of marriage testifies to covenant love rooted in God’s design.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Marriage begins with God’s design, not human invention. From creation, God made man and woman and joined them together in a one-flesh union. This means marriage carries divine meaning, purpose, and accountability.

Marriage is covenantal. It is more than affection, attraction, convenience, or personal fulfillment. Scripture speaks of marriage as a covenant, requiring faithfulness, honor, purity, sacrifice, and commitment before God.

The covenant of marriage also reveals something larger than marriage itself. In Ephesians, the union of husband and wife points to Christ and the church. This does not make every marriage perfect, but it shows that marriage is meant to display faithful love, sacrificial care, and covenant devotion.

Because marriage is holy, it must be guarded from unfaithfulness, selfishness, hardness of heart, abuse, neglect, and impurity. God cares about how husbands and wives treat one another. Marriage is not a place for domination or self-serving control, but for love, honor, truth, and faithfulness under the lordship of Christ.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people today treat marriage as temporary, self-defined, or useful only as long as it satisfies personal desire. Others have experienced deep wounds through betrayal, abandonment, manipulation, or abuse. Scripture gives a higher and holier view: marriage belongs to God and must be shaped by His truth.

This doctrine also protects both the beauty and seriousness of marriage. It honors faithful marriages, calls struggling marriages back to covenant love, and refuses to excuse sin done under the cover of marriage. Christlike faithfulness, not selfish control, is the pattern.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Honor marriage as God’s covenant design. If married, pursue faithfulness, repentance, patience, purity, sacrificial love, and truth in your home. If unmarried, honor marriage without making it an idol. When helping others, do not treat marriage lightly or excuse harm; point people to God’s design, Christ’s love, and wise, faithful obedience.
